content: Polyethylene glycol is a laxative that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of constipation. It is commonly used to relieve occasional constipation or irregularity and typically induces a bowel movement within one to three days. The powder should be dissolved in 4 to 8 ounces of any beverage (cold, hot, or room temperature) and consumed once daily. It is advised not to use this product for more than seven consecutive days unless directed by a healthcare provider. For children aged 16 years or younger, a doctor should be consulted before use. The safety and effectiveness of polyethylene glycol have not been established in pediatric patients. There is also limited information regarding its off-label use in both adult and pediatric populations. Polyethylene glycol should not be used by individuals who are allergic to it. Additionally, it should not be used by patients with kidney disease unless under the supervision of a doctor. Patients experiencing nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks, or those with irritable bowel syndrome should consult a doctor before using this medication. While using polyethylene glycol, it is possible to experience loose, watery, or more frequent stools. If symptoms such as rectal bleeding, worsening nausea, bloating, cramping, or abdominal pain occur, or if diarrhea develops, the medication should be discontinued, and a doctor should be consulted. Prolonged use of a laxative for more than one week is not recommended without medical advice. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should seek guidance from a healthcare professional before using this product. The most commonly reported adverse reactions include diarrhea, flatulence, nausea, and stomach cramps. There is limited information available regarding drug interactions, clinical trial experiences, and postmarketing data for polyethylene glycol. Polyethylene glycol is administered orally. In the event of an overdose, immediate medical attention should be sought, or a Poison Control Center should be contacted at 1-800-222-1222. The active ingredient in each dose is polyethylene glycol 3350, with a dose containing 17 grams of the compound. The product should be stored at a temperature of 20°-25°C (68°-77°F). The tamper-evident foil seal under the cap should be intact before use. There is no established interaction between alcohol and polyethylene glycol, but patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the concurrent use of alcohol with this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name CLEAR LAX®.
